\title{SKILL.md Conformant Sample}

\begin{document}

\maketitle

\section{Explicit grouping}
Bare parentheses do not appear; every delimiter pair uses
\verb|\left|/\verb|\right| as SKILL.md requires:
\begin{equation}
\left( x + y \right)^{2} = x^{2} + 2xy + y^{2}
\end{equation}

\section{Function operators with explicit braces}
Standard operators are scoped with curly braces around their arguments,
and a nested nest of them is used to stress token gluing:
\begin{equation}
\cosh{\ln{\tan{\frac{\varphi}{2}}}}
\end{equation}

Custom operator names use \operatorname{}:
\begin{equation}
\operatorname{rank}(A) = \operatorname{dim}\left( \operatorname{im}\left( A \right) \right)
\end{equation}

A limit with explicit braces around both subscript and argument:
\begin{equation}
\lim_{n \to \infty}{a_{n}} = L
\end{equation}

\section{Structural integrity}
An \verb|align| block for multi-line derivations:
\begin{align}
f(x) &= \sin{\theta} + \cos{\theta} \\
g(x) &= \left( f(x) \right)^{2}
\end{align}

\section{Symbols}
Perpendicularity and multiplication-dot symbols, written as plain macros:
\begin{equation}
u \perp v \qquad a \bullet b
\end{equation}
